text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rebounded 2.7% today after dropping sharply over the prior three trading days, riding a recovery in oil prices as the immediate geopolitical crisis showed signs of stabilization. Brent crude pulled back slightly to $117 following reports that Saudi Arabia's defense minister traveled to Iran to discuss de-escalation, easing some of the panic-driven buying that had pushed prices to six-month highs. For a refiner, this matters: higher crude oil costs cut into profit margins on each gallon refined, so the threat of further Middle East attacks and price spikes had hammered the stock earlier in the week.

The wider picture here is that refiners are caught between two opposing forces. On one hand, geopolitical risk premiums have lifted crude prices, which squeezes refining margins; on the other, U.S. refinery utilization remains robust at 93.4%, meaning there's still solid demand for refined products and the company has inventory flexibility if prices stabilize. Today's bounce reflects investor relief that the conflict may not escalate further—at least not imminently.
